newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Food riots and protests hit Pakistani cities.
newsitem.headline: Food riots and protests hit Pakistani cities.

text.p: Food riots paralysed the northwestern Pakistani city of Peshawar and hit other towns on Monday, forcing the government to order special trains to take wheat there.

Police said they used batons and tear gas in several areas of Peshawar, capital of the North West Frontier Province, to break up demonstrators who looted stocks and blocked roads, protesting against the non-availability of wheat flour for several days.
Food and Agriculture Minister Abida Hussain told parliament in Islamabad that Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif had issued orders for special express trains to transport wheat to the province.

About 5,000 demonstrators, many carrying sticks, looted a state-run utility store in western Peshawar and hundreds tried to attack two flour mills in the west and north of the city on the second days of riots, police said.
Some demonstrators took off their shirts and beat their bare breasts as a mark of protest.
A lorry loaded with flour was looted on a street in the city, where police and protesters played hide and seek for hours, witnesses said.
They said groups of protesters also tried to loot general stores and jewellery shops but were turned away by police.
Demonstrations were also held in several other towns of the province, which borders Afghanistan, and in the southwestern province of Baluchistan, bordering Iran and Afghanistan, residents there said.

The crisis is the first Sharif's government has had to face, coming just six weeks after he took power following the landslide victory of his Pakistan Muslim League party in February 3 general elections.
The government blames the wheat shortage on smuggling to neighbouring countries, particularly to war-shattered Afghanistan, to hoarding and to the late arrival of imported wheat.
In Peshawar, bakeries and traditional ovens supplying the local "nan" flat breads were shut because wheat flour was not available, witnesses said.

A Frontier province government spokesman said after an emergency meeting of the provincial cabinet that the food situation would improve within the next few days with the arrival of fresh wheat supplies from the port city of Karachi.
